precepts.text: Uzzah put forth his hand to the ark when the oxen shook it, and God smote him there for his error; the Most High is serious about what is not to be touched.
precepts.point: That trumpet in the mount was not blown by Moses, for Moses was down among the people sanctifying them; the trumpet came from heaven.

note.label: Exodus 19: The Covenant at Mount Sinai

precepts.why:
At the mount the charge was “There shall not an hand touch it”, and the Most High is serious about that. Here the ark of God was set “upon a new cart”, brought “out of the house of Abinadab that was in Gibeah”, and “Uzzah and Ahio, the sons of Abinadab, drave the new cart.” David and all the house of Israel “played before the Lord on all manner of instruments made of fir wood, even on harps, and on psalteries, and on timbrels, and on cornets, and on cymbals.”

“And when they came to Nachon’s threshingfloor, Uzzah put forth his hand to the ark of God, and took hold of it; for the oxen shook it. And the anger of the Lord was kindled against Uzzah; and God smote him there for his error; and there he died by the ark of God.” The oxen shook the cart and Uzzah put forth his hand and took hold of the ark, and God smote him there.

That is the same charge as the bounds round the mount: what the Most High says is not to be touched is not to be touched, and he will put a man to death for it.

precepts.text: Uzzah took hold of the ark when his family was not chosen for that charge, and God smote him there for his error; he died by the ark of God.
precepts.point: Their charge was the ark, the table, the candlestick, the altars, and the vessels of the sanctuary. Only they were responsible for the ark; anybody outside of that suffered the judgment of the Most High, as Uzzah did generations later when he put forth his hand to the ark and God smote him on the spot.

note.label: Numbers 3: The Levites Taken Instead of the Firstborn

precepts.why:
The ending “ites” denotes the people of; the Kohathites are the people of Kohath, 8,600 males from a month old and upward, pitching on the side of the tabernacle southward. Their charge was “the ark, and the table, and the candlestick, and the altars, and the vessels of the sanctuary wherewith they minister.” Only they were responsible for the ark.

Anybody outside of that suffered the judgment of the Most High, and generations later Uzzah showed it. “And when they came to Nachon’s threshingfloor, Uzzah put forth his hand to the ark of God, and took hold of it; for the oxen shook it. And the anger of the Lord was kindled against Uzzah; and God smote him there for his error; and there he died by the ark of God.”

Uzzah took hold of the ark when his family was not chosen for that charge, and God smote him on the spot. “And David was displeased, because the Lord had made a breach upon Uzzah: and he called the name of the place Perez–uzzah to this day.” The charge of the Kohathites was theirs alone.

precepts.text: The members of the body which seem to be more feeble are necessary; every part in the body has honor.
precepts.point: They set the ark upon a new cart, and Uzzah and Ahio, the sons of Abinadab, drove it, with Ahio going before the ark, while David and all the house of Israel played before the Lord on harps, psalteries, timbrels, cornets, and cymbals.

note.label: 2 Samuel 6: David Brings Up the Ark of God

precepts.why:
“Again, David gathered together all the chosen men of Israel, thirty thousand.” Not everyone is a warrior, and not everyone goes to the front lines. But everyone in the body is important in some way.

“Nay, much more those members of the body, which seem to be more feeble, are necessary.” The members that seem more feeble are needful, and on them more honor is bestowed. Every part in the body has honor.

So it was when David went up from Baale of Judah to bring up the ark of God. There were the chosen men, there were Uzzah and Ahio driving the new cart, and there was “all the house of Israel” playing before the Lord on harps, psalteries, timbrels, cornets and cymbals. Every one had a part.

precepts.text: The LORD said Aaron must not come at all times into the holy place before the mercy seat, that he die not.
precepts.point: David would not remove the ark to the city of David but carried it aside to the house of Obededom the Gittite, where it remained three months; and the Lord blessed Obededom and all his household because of the ark.

note.label: 2 Samuel 6: David Brings Up the Ark of God

precepts.why:
“And the Lord said unto Moses, Speak unto Aaron thy brother, that he come not at all times into the holy place within the vail before the mercy seat, which is upon the ark; that he die not.”

Only chosen men could come near the ark. The Lord set many stipulations upon it, even after the two sons of Aaron died for offering strange fire. Even Aaron, the high priest, could not come before the mercy seat at all times, lest he die. The Most High is holy and not to be handled carelessly.

So when the oxen shook the cart and Uzzah put forth his hand and took hold of the ark, “the anger of the Lord was kindled against Uzzah; and God smote him there for his error.” Grabbing it was a natural reaction, but the Most High had already declared the ark holy and untouchable.

precepts.text: Aaron must put on the holy linen coat and garments and wash his flesh before coming into the holy place.
precepts.point: David would not remove the ark to the city of David but carried it aside to the house of Obededom the Gittite, where it remained three months; and the Lord blessed Obededom and all his household because of the ark.

note.label: 2 Samuel 6: David Brings Up the Ark of God

precepts.why:
Before Aaron could come into the holy place, “He shall put on the holy linen coat, and he shall have the linen breeches upon his flesh, and shall be girded with a linen girdle, and with the linen mitre shall he be attired: these are holy garments; therefore shall he wash his flesh in water, and so put them on.”

Everything in that day had to be done to a T. If the high priest had to be washed and clothed in holy garments before coming near the mercy seat, Uzzah could not lay his hand on the ark at the threshingfloor. The Lord was not playing about his commandments.

We owe thanks that there is mercy through Christ.

precepts.text: My flesh trembleth for fear of thee, and I am afraid of thy judgments; so David feared after Uzzah.
precepts.point: David would not remove the ark to the city of David but carried it aside to the house of Obededom the Gittite, where it remained three months; and the Lord blessed Obededom and all his household because of the ark.

note.label: 2 Samuel 6: David Brings Up the Ark of God

precepts.why:
“My flesh trembleth for fear of thee; and I am afraid of thy judgments.”

So David feared after Uzzah. “David was displeased, because the Lord had made a breach upon Uzzah”, and “David was afraid of the Lord that day, and said, How shall the ark of the Lord come to me?” He had seen the power of the Lord, and his flesh trembled for fear of him and his judgments.

So David would not bring the ark into the city of David, but carried it aside into the house of Obed-edom the Gittite. It stayed there three months, “and the Lord blessed Obed–edom, and all his household” because of the ark.

precepts.text: The shorter account records the same gifts of bread, flesh, and wine to all the people.
precepts.point: David blessed the people in the name of the Most High and dealt to every man and woman a loaf of bread, a piece of flesh, and a flagon of wine.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 16: The Song Delivered into the Hand of Asaph

precepts.why:
The shorter account in Samuel records the same gifts: “he dealt among all the people, even among the whole multitude of Israel, as well to the women as men, to every one a cake of bread, and a good piece of flesh, and a flagon of wine. So all the people departed every one to his house.”

Chronicles says it the same way: when the ark was set in the midst of the tent and the burnt offerings and peace offerings were made, David “blessed the people in the name of the Lord. And he dealt to every one of Israel, both man and woman, to every one a loaf of bread, and a good piece of flesh, and a flagon of wine.”

precepts.text: Michal met David scornfully, David answered that he played before the Most High who chose him over Saul, and she had no child until her death.
precepts.point: Heman and Jeduthun with trumpets and instruments gave thanks because his mercy endureth forever, and all the people departed, and David returned to bless his house.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 16: The Song Delivered into the Hand of Asaph

precepts.why:
Chronicles ends with “David returned to bless his house.” Samuel shows what met him there: “Then David returned to bless his household. And Michal the daughter of Saul came out to meet David”. She met him scornfully: “How glorious was the king of Israel to day, who uncovered himself to day in the eyes of the handmaids of his servants, as one of the vain fellows shamelessly uncovereth himself!”

David answered her, “It was before the Lord, which chose me before thy father, and before all his house, to appoint me ruler over the people of the Lord, over Israel: therefore will I play before the Lord. And I will yet be more vile than thus, and will be base in mine own sight”. He played before the Most High who chose him over Saul.

“Therefore Michal the daughter of Saul had no child unto the day of her death.”

precepts.text: David brought the ark of the Lord and set it in the midst of the tabernacle that he had pitched for it in Jerusalem.
precepts.point: The ark of God had already been brought up by David from Kirjathjearim to the place he had prepared for it, for he had pitched a tent for it at Jerusalem. To read that history, go back to Second Samuel 6, and to First Chronicles 15.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 1: Solomon Asks for Wisdom

precepts.why:
“And they brought in the ark of the Lord, and set it in his place, in the midst of the tabernacle that David had pitched for it: and David offered burnt offerings and peace offerings before the Lord.”

That is the history behind what Chronicles says: “the ark of God had David brought up from Kirjath–jearim to the place which David had prepared for it: for he had pitched a tent for it at Jerusalem.” So in Solomon's day the ark was in the tent David pitched at Jerusalem, while the tabernacle Moses made in the wilderness stood at the high place in Gibeon, where Solomon and the congregation went.

note.label: 2 Samuel 6: David Brings Up the Ark of God

points: David danced before the Lord with all his might, girded with a linen ephod. He was happy and in the spirit, for the Lord had chosen him to bring the ark back among the people. Israel brought up the ark with shouting and the sound of the trumpet.

note.label: 2 Samuel 6: David Brings Up the Ark of God

points: Michal, Saul's daughter, looked through a window and saw David leaping and dancing before the Lord, and she despised him in her heart. This is a spirit to be careful of: coming out of the spirit on the Lord's day and murmuring against a brother who is rejoicing in the Most High.

note.label: 2 Samuel 6: David Brings Up the Ark of God

He dealt to every one, both men and women, a cake of bread, a good piece of flesh, and a flagon of wine, and the people departed to their houses.

note.label: 2 Samuel 6: David Brings Up the Ark of God

points: David returned to bless his own household, still in a good mood. Michal came out to meet him and said sarcastically, How glorious was the king of Israel today, who uncovered himself in the eyes of the handmaids as one of the vain fellows shamelessly uncovereth himself.

She had watched from a distance and could think only of the king dancing with his clothes falling, when the Most High had just brought the ark of God back among Israel. She forgot the greatness of the day and let a murmuring spirit take her.

note.label: 2 Samuel 6: David Brings Up the Ark of God

points: David answered that he danced before the Lord who chose him before her father to be ruler over Israel, therefore he would play before the Lord, and would yet be more vile and base in his own sight, and of the maidservants he would be had in honor.

note.label: 2 Samuel 6: David Brings Up the Ark of God

points: Michal, the daughter of Saul, had no child unto the day of her death; the Lord shut her womb. Do not play with the Most High.
